The mappings are not fixed either: Aquila is rebooked to Utilicorp United on 1/30/01 (263.eml) but Utilicorp United is rebooked to Aquila Risk Management on 3/19/01 (149.eml), and AEP Energy Services, Inc. is 'rebooked' to itself (149.eml). So 15 minutes a day is a guess. Research that could settle it: Count rebook lines across all 71 reports in giron-d/sent and keep only counterparty pairs whose target never changes. Then find mail from book admins or Confirmations (for example Julie Brewer's 'Rebooks' request in 124.eml) showing who rebooks, how long a rebook takes and which lines are the West desk's.
40	- Routing daily Credit Report rebooks to book admins and checking legal entity at deal entry: Credit splits the daily Credit Report by TAGG book and sends each book's lines only to that book's admin, and TAGG/EOL warns or defaults to the legal entity that holds the master agreement when a deal is entered.. Why: The forwarding part is already saved as item 7 in decisions.md and cites the same 71 Giron forwards. The rest repeats claims that earlier critics rejected: no mail shows the other five desk heads forwarding or any admin scanning the list, and the entity mappings the entry check needs change from report to report. Research that could settle it: Find mail from desk heads other than Giron, or from book admins or Confirmations, showing them forwarding the report, picking out their own lines, or rebooking, and how long that takes. Then count, across all 71 reports, the counterparty pairs whose target entity never changes, and size only that.
41	- Self-service counterparty MTM report for audit confirmation requests: Give Confirmations a back-dated counterparty MTM / open-position report (EnTelligence with back-dated curves) so audit requests no longer go to every Risk desk head and analyst.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests' (decisions.md item 1), which cites the same five messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240, 241).
42	- Monthly gas curve validation questions to the desk: Put market-data attribution in the monthly curve validation pack so curves the market explains are marked 'market-explained' and the desk is not asked about them.. Why: The validator already has the market data and says outright that 'the market traded higher' is not an answer she accepts ('as evidenced by the data. However, we are looking for specific reasons', 47.eml), so tagging curves 'market-explained' would not remove the questions; and the 85 minutes a month counts three desk leads and a second round of questions that the mail does not show. Research that could settle it: Find mail from Jennifer Nguyen's validation group or its memo readers saying that a move matching market data needs no desk explanation, and count who actually answers each month (only Giron's replies appear) and how long a reply takes.
43	- Monthly hunt-and-flip of ECC master-swap deals across Houston books: Route deals with ECC master-swap counterparties straight to FT-US/CAND-ERMS in TAGG/EnronOnline, with a nightly exception report, replacing the monthly all-books sweep.. Why: The same work and change are already saved as item 3 in decisions.md, 'Monthly hunt for Enron Canada (ECC) deals in Houston books before NYMEX invoicing', citing the same messages (giron-d/sent/114, 195, 292, 360, 539, 550).
44	- Extending expired deals at flowing HPL meters: A monthly bid-week list of deals ending at meters that still flow, so the Texas desk extends or rolls them in one batch instead of answering per-meter requests after allocation.. Why: The estimate is about three to four times too high: the mail shows roughly 2 distinct extension requests a month, not 5, and the 25 strangers-gas write-off memos are a one-time cleanup of 1999-2000 volumes (21 of them sent between Dec 11 2000 and Jan 9 2001), not a steady 4 a month that the report would prevent. Research that could settle it: Count distinct expired-deal threads per month across farmer-d/logistics after merging forwards (e.g. 782/784/792, 896/897/899, 1479/1482, 58/59/63, 194/195/2149/2150), drop the one-day daily-swing rolls a monthly list cannot catch (814, 1977), and drop the memo backlog unless mail shows new memos for current-month flow after January 2001.
45	- Monthly forward-curve validation questions: Send curve validation questions straight to the owning trader, with threshold commentary entered at month-end, instead of relaying through Gossett and three desk leads.. Why: The relay the proposal removes had already gone away by March 2001, when Nguyen sent her questions straight to Giron with no Gossett forward, and there is no sign that Love or Keiser did any work; what is left is about 10-15 minutes a month of one lead passing a trader's answer along, not 65 minutes. Research that could settle it: Look for curve validation threads in the Love, Keiser, Gossett or Nguyen mailboxes, or for months after March 2001, that show the multi-person relay and repeat rounds still happening; without them only the vague-answer problem is left, and the evidence for that is one second round in one month.
46	- Self-service back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests: Finish the planned EnTelligence view (or an equivalent report) with back-dated curves so Confirmations values counterparty portfolios for a past date without polling every Risk desk.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparty audit requests' (decisions.md item 1), which cites the same five messages (giron-d/sent/136, 137, 214, 240, 241).
47	- Searching all books and flipping ECC third-party deals to FT-US/CAND-ERMS before NYMEX invoicing: Auto-book ECC-mastered counterparty deals to FT-US/CAND-ERMS and replace the all-books request waves with a nightly exception report.. Why: The same work and change are already saved as item 3 in decisions.md, 'Monthly hunt for Enron Canada (ECC) deals in Houston books before NYMEX invoicing', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/108, 195, 270, 292, 360, 539, 550).
48	- Monthly P&L top pages for Arthur Andersen gas testing: Save each gas book's month-end and daily P&L top pages and curve shift reports automatically to a read-only audit folder, with a list of book owners, so AA can pull the pages itself.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as item 4 in decisions.md, "Monthly P&L top pages for Arthur Andersen's gas testing" ($255.00 a month), which cites giron-d/sent/516, 515, 201, 299, 317 and 420.
49	- Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX Access databases: IT runs an unattended overnight compact of every WeaponX file, with a rolling backup and a daily size check, so book admins stop compacting by hand.. Why: The same work and change, citing the same two messages (giron-d/sent/585.eml and 596.eml), is already saved as item 2 in decisions.md, 'Weekly manual compaction of WeaponX Access databases'.
50	- Book ECC-counterparty deals into FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically, with an exception report: Extend the EOL/TAGG auto-booking rule to every ECC-master counterparty and run a nightly exception query instead of manual all-books searches.. Why: The same work and change are already saved as item 3 in decisions.md, 'Monthly hunt for Enron Canada (ECC) deals in Houston books before NYMEX invoicing', which cites most of the same messages; the proposal's estimate was also overstated (single-deal requests counted as all-books searches, and 18 admins per request assumed without support).
51	- Daily Credit Report wrong-entity rebooks and hand-forwarding to book admins: Add standing counterparty-entity rules to TAGG at deal entry and split the Credit Report by desk so it goes straight to each book admin. Why: The 40-minute daily saving rests on claims the mail does not support: only Giron is shown forwarding the report (not six desks), repeat mappings come up about once per report company-wide (not four a day for one desk), and the 'standing rules' are not fixed (Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Holdings is sent to Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Corp on 3/12 but to Louis Dreyfus Corporation on 3/15; ENA/ECC rebooks go both ways), while auto-booking to ECC already exists for some Canadian counterparties. Research that could settle it: Find whether other desk heads (Gossett, Keiser, Love, etc.) also forward the report to admins, and how many lines per report belong to the West book; if not, a resubmission should be limited to adding the West book admin to Credit's distribution list, valued at a few minutes a day.
52	- Hourly phone check-out of service-customer generators to BPA: Replace the hourly calls to Frontier and GCPUD and to BPA with an automatic meter-data feed to BPA and exception alerts to the RT desk.. Why: The mail already says these generators are to be metered automatically, by BPA, from mid-August 2001, and that the hourly calls stop then; so the proposal adds nothing, it treats a short episode as 730 hours a month for good, and its 3-minute figure is a split of a ceiling, not an estimate. Research that could settle it: Look for mail after August 2001 showing the hourly calls to BPA still being made for Frontier or another generator after automatic metering was due, and for what the call actually took each hour; without that the idea is not new and not ongoing.
53	- Monthly Arthur Andersen gas testing document requests: Save each book's daily P&L top page and curve shift report automatically to a dated, read-only folder that the auditors can open themselves.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as item 4 in decisions.md, "Monthly P&L top pages for Arthur Andersen's gas testing" ($255.00 a month), which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/516, 515, 583, 420, 317, 201 and inbox/190).
54	- Weekly California Capacity Report for Transwestern: Have the Friday California capacity email built automatically from flow data and the Gas Daily prices, so the marketer only reviews it.. Why: This work is already saved as 'Weekly Transwestern California Capacity Report' (item 6 in decisions.md, $88.40 a month) and cites the same 16 messages. The draft also had two errors: the 11 Jan 2002 slip sent that week's new figures under the old week's title, not last week's figures, and the unbroken run is 15 weeks, not 16.
55	- Pulling gas P&L top pages and curve-shift reports for Arthur Andersen's monthly testing: Save every book's daily P&L top page and curve-shift report from the nightly P&L run to a dated, read-only folder that the auditors can open, so AA picks its monthly samples itself.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as item 4 in decisions.md, "Monthly P&L top pages for Arthur Andersen's gas testing" ($255.00 a month), which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/583, 516, 515, 420, 317, 201).
56	- Monthly re-pricing of West-desk purchase deals after settlements sees the invoice: Price formula deals (Agave) automatically in Sitara and batch-load the invoice-priced deals (EnerVest #27239, #27253) once a month, so settlements no longer emails the desk lead per deal. Why: For the two invoice-priced deals the price is only known once settlements gets the counterparty's invoice, so a monthly batch still needs settlements to pass each price on and removes almost nothing; the formula part rests on one West Agave miss (the cited Dec 2000 Agave deal is a Central deal), and '3 deals every month' is about three times what the mail shows. Research that could settle it: Check whether the EnerVest #27239 and #27253 contracts price off an index or formula the desk could load before the invoice arrives, and count how many West Agave months were actually wrong in Sitara; if both hold up, a smaller proposal at about one request a month could be argued.
57	- Asking the Texas desk to extend or create a deal when gas flows at a meter with no deal: A nightly list of meters with flow but no active deal, plus a pre-month-end warning about expiring deals at flowing meters, replaces the one-meter-at-a-time emails to the desk lead.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as item 7 in decisions.md, 'Extending Sitara deals for meter flow outside the deal term' (a daily exception list matching meter flow against deal terms), which cites many of the same messages (899, 1021, 1406, 2039, 2049, 2077, 2078, 2095, 2113); the proposal's 12 requests a month was also overstated, as the mail supports about 2 to 3 a month.
58	- Daily hand-forwarding of market reports to Portland traders: Have the daily Energy Market Report and the Gas Daily / Power Daily PDFs delivered straight to Portland distribution lists, so assistants no longer forward them.. Why: The same work and change are already saved as item 8 in decisions.md, 'Hand-forwarding daily market reports to the Portland floor' ($39.95 a month), which cites the same williams-w3 messages; the draft's own figure of 21 times a month at 13 minutes is also not supported, since the archive shows 7 Energy Market Report forwards and only 2 Gas Daily sends in about 9 days.
59	- Monthly Sitara price updates on invoice-priced deals: Let settlements enter the invoiced price or demand charge on flagged invoice-priced Sitara deals themselves, with the desk notified, instead of emailing the desk to key it every month.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as item 11 in decisions.md, 'Monthly Sitara price updates to match counterparty invoices' ($8.50 a month), which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/12, 141, 301, 313, 378, 469, 508, 738, 762, 81).
60	- Re-routing mail sent to the wrong Bill Williams: Give the two Bill Williams directory entries distinct names showing group and city (and, as proposed, distinct SMTP aliases) so senders pick the right one.. Why: The same work and the same fix are already saved as "Forwarding mail sent to the wrong Bill Williams", and most of the cited messages are already there; the proposal also wrongly says both men share one SMTP address, but inbox/141.eml shows Bill III has his own address, bill.williams.III@enron.com.
61	- Daily market report forwarding to Portland traders: Deliver the Energy Market Report and Gas Daily / Power Daily PDFs to maintained distribution lists automatically instead of assistants forwarding them by hand.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as item 9 in decisions.md, 'Hand-forwarding daily market reports to the Portland floor', which cites the same williams-w3 messages.
62	- Monthly wholesale volume variance explanations for Investor Relations: Pre-attribute each region's +/-10% volume variances by driver (EOL vs non-EOL, top counterparties) in the Statistical Database so controllers confirm drafts instead of writing them.. Why: The same work, explaining the monthly Statistical Database variances (farmer-d/logistics/1210.eml and 1416.eml), is already saved in decisions.md as item 6 with a nearly identical pre-fill-and-confirm change, so saving this would count the same savings twice.
63	- Twice-monthly time report email round: Let employees record their own absences directly in the timekeeping system, so the reminder-and-reply email round and the assistant's re-keying go away.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as item 11 in decisions.md, "Pay-period time reports for the Transwestern commercial group", which cites the same Lokay time-report messages.
64	- Monthly gas forward-curve validation questions to desks: Automatically mark curves whose month-over-month shift matches the move in traded market quotes as 'explained by market', and only ask the desks about the rest. Why: The mail shows the validator already sees the market move in the data and explicitly rejects 'the market traded higher' as an answer, asking instead for the specific reasons behind it, so a market-move check would not remove the questions. Research that could settle it: Only a source showing Risk would accept a quote-based match as enough to close a curve question (for example a validation policy or a memo accepting such answers) could change this; the current thread says the opposite.
65	- Monthly requests to re-price invoice-priced deals in Sitara: Keep a standing list of deals re-priced every month (EnerVest S#27239, #27253, Agave #312068) and have the book admin update them at month start without being asked, with formula pricing where the calculation is known.. Why: The same work is already saved as item 14 in decisions.md, 'Monthly Sitara price updates to match counterparty invoices', which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/12, 81, 301, 313, 378, 469, 508), and a nearly identical batch-and-formula version was already rejected (item 54) because invoice-driven prices still need settlements to pass each one on.
66	- Forwarding mail sent to the wrong Bill Williams: Add each person's group to the two "Bill Williams" address book names so senders can see which one they are picking.. Why: The same work and the same fix are already saved as item 13 in decisions.md, 'Forwarding mail sent to the wrong Bill Williams' ($15.30 a month), which cites most of the same williams-w3 sent_items messages.
67	- Routing items for the daily imbalance check to its owner: Name one owner and backup for the daily imbalance check and send inputs to a shared mailbox that reaches them, so items are no longer hand-carried to the right person.. Why: The mail shows two misrouted items in two days (15 and 16 Nov 2001), each already fixed by a one-line 'send it to X going forward' note; nothing shows misrouting happening every business day, so this is a short ownership mix-up that ends, not daily recurring work. Research that could settle it: Look for more messages over several weeks or months where imbalance-check items are forwarded, walked over, or redirected between Giron, Poorman, Williams and Lokay after 16 Nov 2001; without them, no rate of misrouting can be supported.
68	- Daily hand-forwarding of market reports to Portland traders: Deliver the daily Energy Market Report and the Gas Daily/Power Daily PDFs straight to Portland distribution lists, ending the assistants' daily hand-forwarding.. Why: The same work and change are already saved as item 10 in decisions.md, 'Hand-forwarding daily market reports to the Portland floor' ($39.95 a month), citing the same williams-w3 messages; the draft's 8 minutes every business day for Gas Daily/Power Daily is also unsupported, since Bill Williams's dense 1/28-2/6 inbox holds all 7 Energy Market Report forwards but only one Gas Daily/Power Daily send (1/31) and one 'not loaded yet' note (2/4).
69	- Monthly Investor Relations volume-variance explanations: Pre-draft each region's volume-variance explanation from a system breakdown (EnronOnline vs. other deals, top counterparty changes) so desk contacts only confirm or edit it.. Why: The only replies in the mail are one-line answers from a single contact (Baumbach), which suggests minutes of work, not the assumed 20 minutes of research for each of 11 contacts, so the 15 minutes saved per contact is not supported. Research that could settle it: Find replies from the other contacts (Bruce, Gossett, Keiser, Kelly, Etter, Scott, Louie, Confer, Leschber, Anderson) or follow-ups from Misti Day showing long explanations, missed deadlines or back-and-forth over drivers. That would show real research time beyond a one-line answer.
70	- Purchase requisition work handled by one logistics analyst: Move routine requisitions to an SAP/catalog workflow with electronic approval and requester goods-receipt, and name a backup for Mary Poorman. Why: The only evidence is a single offhand line from Mary Poorman that never says what her requisition steps are; the one requisition shown (237.eml) already goes through an online ECT Hardware Request form with an SAP cost center and electronic manager approval, so the proposed fix may already exist; and the 25% saving is an assumption with nothing behind it. Research that could settle it: Find mail that shows Mary Poorman's actual requisition steps (what she re-keys, which approvals or receipts she chases, how many requisitions a week) and whether they go outside the existing ECT request/SAP system; without that, neither the change nor the minutes can be stated.
71	- Monthly Wholesale volume variance explanations: Have the Statistical Database show each region's volume change split by EnronOnline vs. other deals and top counterparties, so desk contacts confirm rather than research.. Why: The same work, from the same two messages (farmer-d/logistics/1210.eml and 1416.eml), is already saved as item 7 in decisions.md, 'Monthly wholesale-volume variance explanations for Investor Relations' ($184.45 a month), with an essentially equivalent pre-fill-and-confirm change.
72	- Houston Pipe Line Assignment, Termination, Expiration Report: Generate the report automatically from Global Contracts on a schedule and let recipients subscribe themselves, instead of Cheryl Dudley compiling it and keeping the distribution list by hand.. Why: The mail shows a monthly report (titled 03/01 and 04/01), not two a month: the 8 March issue was a one-time catch-up for a missed March report, and 2133.eml is the same 23 March message as 211.eml. Nothing in the mail shows that the report is put together by hand rather than printed from Global, and no add or remove requests for the list appear, so the time saved per report has no support. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing how the report is produced (a manual compilation or a Global printout), more issues of it to set the real frequency, and any add or remove requests for the list.
73	- Monthly OPM hours survey entry in the Access tool: Pre-fill each cost center's hours by activity and commercial-team percentage splits with last month's values so managers only edit what changed.. Why: The mail never shows managers re-entering unchanged hours or team splits in the Access tool: it says commercial teams and FTEs roll over each month, shows prior-month hours in a report, and says nothing about how hours are entered or how long it takes, so the 8 minutes x 37 managers and the 2 split follow-ups a month (the mailbox shows one in Oct 2000 and one in Aug 2001, both caused by a missing prompt rather than re-entry) are guesses. Research that could settle it: Find mail from the OPM team (Suzanne Nicholie, Shari Mao, Roxanne Saldana) or a manager after February 2001 that says whether the Access entry screen starts blank or with last month's hours, whether team percentages must be re-entered each month, and how long a manager spends on the survey; also count split follow-ups like 84.eml and 1447.eml across other mailboxes.
74	- Liquidation flash support from the desks: Have the month-end liquidations run write each region's deal-level liquidation support into ERMS/1Intra/FRED Liquidations/<year>/<month> so Jim Little no longer requests it from the desks.. Why: The mail shows one catch-up episode, not a monthly task for four regions: the only two requests (27 Feb and 29 Mar 2001) chase November, December and January 2000-01 support, the March message is a follow-up on the same December backlog, no request appears for any later month-end even though Giron's sent mail runs to June 2001, and 345.eml says ERMS cannot produce support for the transport liquidations, which are part of what was asked for. Research that could settle it: Look for liquidation-support requests or saves to the FRED Liquidations folder for month-ends after January 2001, from Phillip Love's, Patrick Ryder's or Jim Little's mailboxes, showing the request repeats every month for each region, and check whether the non-transport support (like Anne Bike's index-position file in 345.eml) is already produced routinely.
75	- Monthly Sitara price and demand-charge updates to match invoices: Let settlements analysts enter the invoiced price or demand charge themselves on deals flagged as invoice-priced, with every change logged for the desk to review.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved in decisions.md as 'Monthly Sitara price updates to match counterparty invoices' ($8.50 a month), which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/12, 141, 301, 313, 378, 469, 508, 738, 762, 81).
76	- Collecting biweekly time reports by email (Transwestern commercial group): Have each person record their own time off in the timekeeping system when it happens, so the assistant only reviews a list of exceptions instead of collecting email replies.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved in decisions.md as "Pay-period time reports for the Transwestern commercial group", which cites the same Lokay time-report messages.
77	- Monthly accounting arrangement for meter 98-7266 (TGLO storage fuel at Bammel): Replace the hand-built monthly accounting arrangement for meter 7266 with a standing evergreen deal pair on contracts 012-41500-05-002 and 012-88494-05-001.. Why: The mail shows only two moments 20 months apart, does not show the monthly hand-build still happening in 2001 (Farmer was asked for a deal in Feb 2000), and by May 2001 the contracts were 'canceled or expired', so the October 2001 entry looks like cleanup after the storage flow ended, not ongoing monthly work. Research that could settle it: Look for mail after February 2000 showing whether Farmer set up the requested deal for 7266, and for any 7266 or TGLO Bammel storage volumes in months after May 2001; if neither exists, the work has ended and the idea fails.
78	- Waiting on Path Confirmation saves during nightly checkouts: Make Path Confirmation save confirmations in the background (or in one commit per counterparty) so the shift trader does not wait about a minute per save.. Why: The same work, the nightly Path Confirmation checkouts with the same background-save fix and the same messages (williams-w3/sent_items/86.eml and 62.eml), is already saved as item 2 in decisions.md.
79	- Wellhead spot/interim ticket requests to logistics: Producer Services enters wellhead spot and interim tickets in Sitara directly instead of emailing the terms to Texas logistics to type in.. Why: The mail shows about 9 requests in 7 months (about 1.3 a month, not 3) and only one bid-week list, not one a month. One cited 'resend' is really a new deal. It is also not shown that Producer Services can or may enter spot tickets: when asked to enter one directly, they passed it to logistics instead. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing Producer Services entering spot or interim tickets in Sitara themselves, or a rule that keeps deal entry away from the people who negotiate the deal. Also look for more bid-week spot lists or ticket requests in other mailboxes that would raise the real count.
80	- Nightly real-time schedule checkout calls: Auto-match Enpower prescheduled paths against OATI e-tags so traders call only counterparties whose paths do not match. Why: The mail shows the tag record Enron sees is incomplete and that the nightly calls are what catch the problems, so matching against tags cannot safely replace the calls, and the claim that two thirds of calls would go away has no support. Research that could settle it: Mail showing that, over a normal stretch of weeks, Enron's tag data matched what counterparties actually scheduled, and how many paths and calls a typical night's checkout involved, could support a narrower version that only skips the manual save step for paths that match.
81

Group,

Cuts are on the way. While most can be zeroed out in Enpower (for LD's) like normal, longterm contracts will require an annuity for the value of the cut on that particular day. In the interest of being uniform, the guidelines for cuts are below. 

We will be handling cuts in the following manner:

1. Documentation is priority #1. We need to fill out a cut sheet with the times, the name of the person who called, the tag number, the quantity and price.

2. After attempting to resupply the cut or find an alternate sink we need to carefully document changes in the new enpower workspace.

3. We need to zero out all cut deals in Enpower, we then need to calculate the value of the deals and make an annuity. The annuity must be made HE 1 on the following day of the schedule. The annuity needs to be for 1 mw for the value of the zeroed out contract. In the comment section of the annuity you must include the Enpower deal # of the cut deal and should include an indication of the number of mws each hour and the contract price--for example (4 hours @ 25 mws X $100 per mw = $10,000).

4. Please be as accurate as possible. We still need to be flat in Enpower at the end of each day. And we still need to calculate our daily position.

5. Put all cut sheets in the accordion folder on Kate Symes' Desk.

I appreciate your help and diligence.
Thanks,

Bill

content.text: I'm still working. A search for evidence that could revive the rejected Calpine proposal found no scheduler replies to Calpine, so it stays dropped. I'm checking the critic's verdict on TECO.

I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection. There are two separate problems: the same work is already saved, and several claims don't match the mail.

**1. The work is already saved.** Item 10 in `decisions.md`, "Extending Sitara deals for meter flow outside the deal term", covers the same job. Settlements or volume management finds gas flowing at a meter with no current deal and emails the desk to extend it. That saved proposal already cites `2095.eml` from this TECO thread. Its daily list of meters whose flow falls outside a deal's dates would also catch the TECO lapses, so saving this one would count the same savings twice.

**2. Evidence errors that would need fixing in any resubmission:**
- **983.eml is not a March 2000 lapse.** It is a March 2000 forward. The quoted lines ("I DID NOT see a TECO deal ticket in MOPS", "12-86978-101 NEEDED") are from April 1999, when HPLC's deal was first being set up.
- **The episode count is too high.** 2093, 2095 and 2099 were all sent on 23 Feb 2001 and are one episode, not two. The real lapse episodes are:
  - June 2000 (`1626.eml`)
  - 23 Feb 2001 (2093/2095/2099); the next working day's `2103.eml` refers to an El Paso deal, 637225, made "last Friday" to replace it
  - April 2001 (194/195/2149/2150)
  - July 2001 (`95.eml`), which the proposal missed. Here 637225 had lapsed for April and May, and Megan Parker's request went unanswered for 17 days.
- **The person who would have to paper the arrangement declined.** The proposal cites Weissman's "9 more years" but leaves out that in the same message he says he is "reluctant to open this can of worms" (`1626.eml`). The mail also shows the arrangement was partly papered at times: a 1996 HPLR contract, and a Committed Reserves Agreement dated 12/1/98. So "never put on paper" overstates it.
- **The counterparty-merge fix is unsupported.** No message says how a name change should be handled. The mail only shows the suspended counterparty blocking an extension and a new deal being booked in its place (`2095.eml`, `2103.eml`).

**What could fix it.** The idea isn't hopeless; the problem is the overlap and the evidence. A resubmission would need to:
- show what the saved meter-flow list would not catch here, for example that this buy/sell pair needs a new ticket rather than an extension;
- use the four real episodes over about 14 months, roughly 0.3 a month, which is still only about $20 a month;
- check whether the desk could book long-term tickets itself, without the papering Weissman declined.

input.description: Proposal: single buyback/deficiency report from Sitara
input.prompt:
Proposal: Record industrial buyback, swing and deficiency terms on the Sitara deal tickets and produce one monthly "Buyback & Deficiency" report from Sitara, replacing the separate hand-kept lists (Julie Meyers' monthly spreadsheet, the scheduler's monthly buyback list, and the industrial worksheet/report) that are compared against each other each month.

TODAY: Each month at least two, sometimes three, people keep overlapping lists of which HPL industrial customers have buyback/swing/deficiency arrangements. Julie Meyers (contracts) emails an "UPDATED SPREADSHEET" monthly to about 13 people. The industrial scheduler (Ken Seaman, later Robert Lloyd) builds a monthly buyback list and asks Julie to check it against hers, and also keeps a monthly industrial report/worksheet for Gas Control, Logistics and the on-call scheduler. The successor has to ask Julie for her worksheet to build his own. Because the terms are not on the deal tickets, people can't tell from Sitara whether a buyback is active, the industrial report lapses for months, and buyback and swing tickets get set up late, by the 3rd working day, while gas flows.
Evidence:
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/601.eml (Dec 20 1999), Howard Camp: "a buyback is set up until June 2000 per Julie Meyers notes she sends out every month ( Last note sent Dec 3 and you are on distribution list)" … "Do we have an active buyback in place and how do you decide to use the buyback?" … "If not, please notify Julie and note on the deal ticket that this buyback is no longer effective."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/645.eml (Jan 4 2000), Ken Seaman to Lloyd and Meyers: "Attached are the current buyback deals I'm aware of. If you have further information please let me know."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/759.eml (Feb 7 2000), Seaman: "Attached is my list for Feb. Please let me know if you see anything out of the ordinary."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1078.eml (Apr 28 2000), Meyers to 13 people, "UPDATED SPREADSHEET": "Here are the updates for May. You will notice I have not added the extra deals for Equistar Chemical because it didn't effect the whole month, plus I only found the split out for the sale upto 4/00 not the purchase."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/852.eml (Feb 2000), Farmer: "Ken developed an industrial report before he left. It can be found at o/logistics/kenseaman/industrialsmonthly/... There is one file for each month of 2000. I need you to update this for March. This will need to be distributed to Gas Control, Logistics, and myself." Lloyd to Meyers: "Can you please forward me the "Buyback/Deficiency" Deals for March' 2000. Your worksheet would greatly assist me with completing this request."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1253.eml (Jun 28–29 2000), Farmer: "When will the buybacks and swings be set up for July? … I believe that we agreed that these would be set up by the 3rd work day, which would be Friday the 7th. (Six days of flow.)" and "we need to get the Industrial spreadsheet up and running again. This report is very beneficial to Gas Control, industrial traders and schedulers on call." Lloyd: "I will finalize my pathing tomorrow, Thursday, and set up buybacks and swings by the end of day Friday." / "I will have a preliminary worksheet done by the end of day Friday." Pat Clynes: "Please make sure that Gary gets a copy of the Industrial spreadsheet. Nobody has seen it in a few months."

CHANGE: Add buyback/swing/deficiency fields (effective dates, pricing basis, active flag) to the industrial base sales tickets in Sitara, maintained by contracts when a deal is papered or changed. A standard Sitara report run on the 1st replaces Julie's spreadsheet, the scheduler's buyback list and the industrial worksheet, and goes automatically to Gas Control, Logistics, the on-call scheduler and Client Services.

AFTER: One source of truth. No monthly compare-and-confirm between two lists, no asking for the other person's worksheet, no lapsed industrial report. Buyback/swing setup starts on day 1 from the report instead of waiting for the lists to be reconciled.

ESTIMATE (conservative, per month): Julie updating and emailing her spreadsheet about 45 min. Scheduler building his separate buyback list and reconciling it with Julie's about 45 min. Building and distributing the industrial worksheet/report about 45 min. Chasers and questions about whether a buyback is active (601, 852, 1253) about 20 min. Total about 155 min; afterwards about 25 min for contracts to keep the deal fields current and someone to glance at the report = about 130 min/month ≈ 2.2 h × $85 ≈ $184/month. The economic cost of setting up buybacks/swings on the 3rd working day ("Six days of flow") is not counted. 25	 To path a buyback {MOP; Supply List}  with an existing Market Deal 
26	{typically baseload} please follow these steps:
27	  
28	 Theory # 1:   Example; Supply Deal = 5.0/d  & Market Deal = 5.0/d
29	 
30	  1.) Attach the Supply Deal with the Market Deal to establish a "buy/sell"  
31	path list contract  oppose to a transport contract.
32	
33	  2.) Path the transaction on the "buy/sell" { or broker the deal}  contract.
34	 
35	  3.) This process is applicable only if the Supply Deal and the Market Deal 
36	are the same quantity.
37	 
38	  4.) This example will yield a net zero activity in POP.
39	  
40	 Theory # 2:  Example ;   Supply Deal = 7.0/d  &  Market Deal = 10.0/d
41	 
42	  1)  Follow  steps 1 & 2 in Theory # 1.
43	 
44	  2.) Additionally, create a service transportation contract {i.e. K-215}  in 
45	the path list.
46	 
47	  2.) Path 7.0 on the "buy/sell" path list contract and  10.0  on the 
48	transport {i.e. K-215} contract.
49	  
50	 This procedure will eliminate  an out-of-balance in MOP for both the "Supply 
51	Deal and the Market Deal"  and send 3.0  to POP via x-port K-215.
52	 
53	 Note:  Never path a buyback {Supply Deal}  using a receipt transport contact 
54	and the{ Market Deal}  using  a  delivery transport contract.
55	  
56	  POP's should only  reflect  the "net" on these two transactions {buyback 
57	and baseload deal}.

It is done about twice a month, around the 8th–15th and again before bid week. Because it is manual, a cycle was missed entirely when an earlier revision ran late. The distribution list is also maintained by hand, by asking recipients to email or phone in changes.
Evidence:
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2114.eml (Mar 8 2001), to about 40 recipients: "Since I did the revision to the February 2001 report so late last month, I accidentally failed to do the report for March 2001. Attached is a report for March 2001 which covers all assignments, terminations & expirations entered since the last report was done on 2/15/01. (FYI - It contains all of the entries made by our group since the report was last done on 3/8/01, regardless of the effective date.) If you do not need to receive this report or if you know of someone else that should receive it, please let me know by e-mail or phone (x-36982) so that I can either remove your name from or add their name to the distribution list."
The cadence in these messages (2/15, the missed early-March report done 3/8, 3/22–23 before bid week) is about twice a month.

CHANGE: A saved query in the contract system (Global Contracts) selects every assignment, termination and expiration entered since the last run date. It runs on the 15th and on the business day before bid week, and publishes to a shared folder or a mail distribution group that recipients join or leave themselves.

AFTER: The report goes out on schedule without anyone compiling it, cycles can't be skipped, and list maintenance is self-service. Contract Administration only checks the output.

ESTIMATE (conservative): Compiling entries since the last run, formatting and sending about 40 min per report, plus about 5 min of list-maintenance requests. Afterwards about 10 min to check the auto-generated output, so about 35 min saved per report. At about 2 reports a month that is about 70 min/month ≈ 1.2 h × $85 ≈ $99/month. If you prefer to count only the two dated reports, about 1 a month, it is about 35 min/month ≈ $50/month. The value of not missing a cycle (2114.eml) is not counted.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded it in `decisions.md`. The rejection file is `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-4\proposals\buyback-deficiency-report-reject.json`. No one else has saved or rejected this work.

The quotes are accurate and the work does happen monthly. Julie Meyers' "UPDATED SPREADSHEET" went to the same 13 people in Jan 2000 (650.eml) and Apr 2000 (1078.eml). But the way the proposal describes the work is wrong in three places, and the savings estimate depends on them.

**1. There are two lists, not three, so one 45-minute item is counted twice.**
- In January and February, Ken Seaman sent his buyback list to Julie and Robert Lloyd (645, 759).
- After Ken left, Lloyd took over Ken's "industrial report." To build it he asked Julie for her "Buyback/Deficiency" worksheet (852).
- In 1253 that same document is called the industrial "Buyback & Deficiency Deals" worksheet.

So the scheduler's buyback list and the industrial worksheet are one document. The mail also shows no monthly comparison of two independent lists after February. From March on, Lloyd built his worksheet from Julie's.

**2. The mail partly contradicts the starting premise.**
The proposal says the terms are not on the deal tickets. In 601.eml, Howard Camp asks Lee to "note on the deal ticket that this buyback is no longer effective." That suggests buyback status is already recorded on tickets in some form. The proposal needs to show what Sitara is actually missing.

**3. The claim that setup would start on day 1 has no support.**
Farmer's "3rd work day" deadline in 1253 is an agreed target. Lloyd says the setup waits on his pathing: "I will finalize my pathing tomorrow … and set up buybacks and swings by the end of day Friday." Nothing ties the delay to comparing lists, and a report would not set up tickets.

**Smaller problems**
- The worksheet "lapsed for months" (1253: "Nobody has seen it in a few months"). In those months nobody spent the 45 minutes, so it can't be counted as saved every month. Nothing shows that the lapse came from the terms being missing from tickets.
- Julie's monthly upkeep doesn't go away. It moves into keeping the ticket fields current.

**Verdict**
The problem is mainly the evidence and the estimate, not the idea. A single source that the scheduler doesn't have to rebuild each month could be a valid, smaller proposal, but the real saving is probably 30–45 minutes a month, not 130.

**Research that could settle it**
- What Julie's spreadsheet actually contains. The mail never says, though 601 and 852 suggest it is the buyback/deficiency list.
- Whether Sitara tickets already carry buyback terms or notes.
- How many months the industrial worksheet was actually produced.

A resubmission should then estimate only the scheduler's monthly rebuild and drop the day-1 setup claim.

70	- Monthly Investor Relations volume-variance explanations: Pre-draft each region's volume-variance explanation from a system breakdown (EnronOnline vs. other deals, top counterparty changes) so desk contacts only confirm or edit it.. Why: The only replies in the mail are one-line answers from a single contact (Baumbach), which suggests minutes of work, not the assumed 20 minutes of research for each of 11 contacts, so the 15 minutes saved per contact is not supported. Research that could settle it: Find replies from the other contacts (Bruce, Gossett, Keiser, Kelly, Etter, Scott, Louie, Confer, Leschber, Anderson) or follow-ups from Misti Day showing long explanations, missed deadlines or back-and-forth over drivers. That would show real research time beyond a one-line answer.
71	- Purchase requisition work handled by one logistics analyst: Move routine requisitions to an SAP/catalog workflow with electronic approval and requester goods-receipt, and name a backup for Mary Poorman. Why: The only evidence is a single offhand line from Mary Poorman that never says what her requisition steps are; the one requisition shown (237.eml) already goes through an online ECT Hardware Request form with an SAP cost center and electronic manager approval, so the proposed fix may already exist; and the 25% saving is an assumption with nothing behind it. Research that could settle it: Find mail that shows Mary Poorman's actual requisition steps (what she re-keys, which approvals or receipts she chases, how many requisitions a week) and whether they go outside the existing ECT request/SAP system; without that, neither the change nor the minutes can be stated.
72	- Monthly Wholesale volume variance explanations: Have the Statistical Database show each region's volume change split by EnronOnline vs. other deals and top counterparties, so desk contacts confirm rather than research.. Why: The same work, from the same two messages (farmer-d/logistics/1210.eml and 1416.eml), is already saved as item 7 in decisions.md, 'Monthly wholesale-volume variance explanations for Investor Relations' ($184.45 a month), with an essentially equivalent pre-fill-and-confirm change.
73	- Houston Pipe Line Assignment, Termination, Expiration Report: Generate the report automatically from Global Contracts on a schedule and let recipients subscribe themselves, instead of Cheryl Dudley compiling it and keeping the distribution list by hand.. Why: The mail shows a monthly report (titled 03/01 and 04/01), not two a month: the 8 March issue was a one-time catch-up for a missed March report, and 2133.eml is the same 23 March message as 211.eml. Nothing in the mail shows that the report is put together by hand rather than printed from Global, and no add or remove requests for the list appear, so the time saved per report has no support. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing how the report is produced (a manual compilation or a Global printout), more issues of it to set the real frequency, and any add or remove requests for the list.
74	- Monthly OPM hours survey entry in the Access tool: Pre-fill each cost center's hours by activity and commercial-team percentage splits with last month's values so managers only edit what changed.. Why: The mail never shows managers re-entering unchanged hours or team splits in the Access tool: it says commercial teams and FTEs roll over each month, shows prior-month hours in a report, and says nothing about how hours are entered or how long it takes, so the 8 minutes x 37 managers and the 2 split follow-ups a month (the mailbox shows one in Oct 2000 and one in Aug 2001, both caused by a missing prompt rather than re-entry) are guesses. Research that could settle it: Find mail from the OPM team (Suzanne Nicholie, Shari Mao, Roxanne Saldana) or a manager after February 2001 that says whether the Access entry screen starts blank or with last month's hours, whether team percentages must be re-entered each month, and how long a manager spends on the survey; also count split follow-ups like 84.eml and 1447.eml across other mailboxes.
75	- Liquidation flash support from the desks: Have the month-end liquidations run write each region's deal-level liquidation support into ERMS/1Intra/FRED Liquidations/<year>/<month> so Jim Little no longer requests it from the desks.. Why: The mail shows one catch-up episode, not a monthly task for four regions: the only two requests (27 Feb and 29 Mar 2001) chase November, December and January 2000-01 support, the March message is a follow-up on the same December backlog, no request appears for any later month-end even though Giron's sent mail runs to June 2001, and 345.eml says ERMS cannot produce support for the transport liquidations, which are part of what was asked for. Research that could settle it: Look for liquidation-support requests or saves to the FRED Liquidations folder for month-ends after January 2001, from Phillip Love's, Patrick Ryder's or Jim Little's mailboxes, showing the request repeats every month for each region, and check whether the non-transport support (like Anne Bike's index-position file in 345.eml) is already produced routinely.
76	- Monthly Sitara price and demand-charge updates to match invoices: Let settlements analysts enter the invoiced price or demand charge themselves on deals flagged as invoice-priced, with every change logged for the desk to review.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved in decisions.md as 'Monthly Sitara price updates to match counterparty invoices' ($8.50 a month), which cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/12, 141, 301, 313, 378, 469, 508, 738, 762, 81).
77	- Collecting biweekly time reports by email (Transwestern commercial group): Have each person record their own time off in the timekeeping system when it happens, so the assistant only reviews a list of exceptions instead of collecting email replies.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved in decisions.md as "Pay-period time reports for the Transwestern commercial group", which cites the same Lokay time-report messages.
78	- Monthly accounting arrangement for meter 98-7266 (TGLO storage fuel at Bammel): Replace the hand-built monthly accounting arrangement for meter 7266 with a standing evergreen deal pair on contracts 012-41500-05-002 and 012-88494-05-001.. Why: The mail shows only two moments 20 months apart, does not show the monthly hand-build still happening in 2001 (Farmer was asked for a deal in Feb 2000), and by May 2001 the contracts were 'canceled or expired', so the October 2001 entry looks like cleanup after the storage flow ended, not ongoing monthly work. Research that could settle it: Look for mail after February 2000 showing whether Farmer set up the requested deal for 7266, and for any 7266 or TGLO Bammel storage volumes in months after May 2001; if neither exists, the work has ended and the idea fails.
79	- Waiting on Path Confirmation saves during nightly checkouts: Make Path Confirmation save confirmations in the background (or in one commit per counterparty) so the shift trader does not wait about a minute per save.. Why: The same work, the nightly Path Confirmation checkouts with the same background-save fix and the same messages (williams-w3/sent_items/86.eml and 62.eml), is already saved as item 2 in decisions.md.
80	- Wellhead spot/interim ticket requests to logistics: Producer Services enters wellhead spot and interim tickets in Sitara directly instead of emailing the terms to Texas logistics to type in.. Why: The mail shows about 9 requests in 7 months (about 1.3 a month, not 3) and only one bid-week list, not one a month. One cited 'resend' is really a new deal. It is also not shown that Producer Services can or may enter spot tickets: when asked to enter one directly, they passed it to logistics instead. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing Producer Services entering spot or interim tickets in Sitara themselves, or a rule that keeps deal entry away from the people who negotiate the deal. Also look for more bid-week spot lists or ticket requests in other mailboxes that would raise the real count.
81	- Nightly real-time schedule checkout calls: Auto-match Enpower prescheduled paths against OATI e-tags so traders call only counterparties whose paths do not match. Why: The mail shows the tag record Enron sees is incomplete and that the nightly calls are what catch the problems, so matching against tags cannot safely replace the calls, and the claim that two thirds of calls would go away has no support. Research that could settle it: Mail showing that, over a normal stretch of weeks, Enron's tag data matched what counterparties actually scheduled, and how many paths and calls a typical night's checkout involved, could support a narrower version that only skips the manual save step for paths that match.
82	- Re-extending the TECO / El Paso Seven Oaks buy/sell tickets at meter 6884: Paper the Seven Oaks tailgate adjustment and book one evergreen purchase and one evergreen sale ticket at meter 6884, instead of extending or re-creating the tickets by email whenever settlements finds them expired.. Why: The work is a case of item 10 already saved in decisions.md ('Extending Sitara deals for meter flow outside the deal term'), which already cites 2095.eml from this thread, so saving it would count the same savings twice. The evidence also has errors: 983.eml's quotes are from April 1999 setup mail, not a March 2000 lapse; 2093/2095 and 2099 are one episode on 23 Feb 2001, not two; the proposal leaves out that George Weissman, who would have to paper it, said he was 'reluctant to open this can of worms' (1626.eml); and the counterparty-merge fix has nothing in the mail behind it. Research that could settle it: Show what the saved meter-flow exception list would not catch here, for example that 6884's buy/sell pair needs a new ticket rather than an extension. Count the real episodes: Jun 2000 (1626), 23 Feb 2001 (2093/2095/2099, replaced by El Paso deal 637225 in 2103), Apr 2001 (194/195/2149/2150), and Jul 2001 (95.eml, where 637225 had lapsed again). Find out whether the desk could book long-term tickets without the paper Weissman declined to draw up.
83	- Night-shift emailing of the daily EES and EPE model files: Email the nightly EES model and daily EPE model automatically from their save folders to maintained distribution lists instead of traders sending them by hand.. Why: The 2-sends-a-day rate is not supported: EES model mail appears only in June 2001 and EPE model mail only from December 2001, so the two never run together; the EES recipient fix (the EES Power Settlements list) already existed and was already in use; and what is left, one attachment to one address a night, saves about a minute or two. Research that could settle it: Find EES model sends after June 2001 that run alongside the EPE model, or EPE model mail showing real time or trouble per send (late, wrong or missing models, recipient changes, El Paso chasing a day), and check that the EPE work went on after the estate took over in February 2002.
84	- Long/short position hand-off emails to the Portland Real Time shift: Replace the hand-typed 'we are long/short' emails with an Enpower report of each book's open positions for Real Time to fill.. Why: The proposed report already exists: Real Time's position manager already shows each book's long/short by point and hour (183.eml: 'You will see us short this amount in the RT position manager'), so what the emails add is instruction (where to fill, what to do with it, price, which deal links), which Enpower deal data does not hold; and in 120.eml Enpower itself was wrong, so an Enpower-fed report would have carried the same error. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing Real Time traders re-keying or cross-checking hand-off emails against Enpower and how long that takes, and see whether the planned FSP consolidated position manager (167.eml) already covers it; a resubmission would have to target the instruction part (for example a fill-note field on the deal in Enpower) and count hand-offs from the preschedulers' mailboxes, not Bill's forwards.
85	- Second, unposted TW Current Shipper rate matrix: Ask the recipients once whether anyone uses the second matrix and, if no one does, stop updating and sending it.. Why: The archive shows this work only once (the November 2001 rate change), so the assumed rate of a change every other month has no support, and the 20 minutes of re-keying is a guess for a file whose effort the mail never describes. Research that could settle it: Find other TW rate matrix postings or Current Shipper rate changes (for example other MATRIX<yyyymm> files, Global Settlement rate or TCR surcharge updates, or other mail from Rita Bianchi) that show how often these rates change.
86	- Monthly analyst (A&A) RC charges and RC-owner checks: Generate the $6,400-per-analyst journal entry from the Org Database automatically and email only RC owners whose analyst count changed, instead of asking all 63 to check monthly.. Why: The errors the mail reports are analysts who left while the Org Database still listed them, so their count never changes and a change-only notice would miss exactly those errors; the savings also rest on unsupported figures (all 63 recipients checking monthly, a 45-minute manual entry) drawn from two setup messages in early 2000. Research that could settle it: Look for later months' A&A charge or reclass mail showing how many RCs actually hold analysts, how often reclasses are needed, and how long Financial Operations spends on the entry; a revised idea would need a check that catches stale database records, such as matching against HR terminations or transfers.
87	- Monthly counterparty name change/merger notices to ~170 people: Send each counterparty name change or merger only to people with active deals or contracts with that counterparty, and post the full list on the intranet.. Why: The 150 minutes saved per notice rests on two guesses the mail does not show: that most of the ~170 recipients are not affected, and that each spends a minute checking. The notices hold no list, and the mail suggests a name change affects scheduling and volume systems widely (1016.eml). The 584.eml evidence also points the other way: that notice went to a narrow list and still had to be forwarded by hand to three schedulers who were not on it. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing which recipient groups actually act on these notices and which ignore them (replies, objections, or 'take me off this list' requests), how many counterparties a typical monthly list holds, and whether Sitara/Global Contracts can map a counterparty to the people who need to know, including schedulers whose EDI and Unify paths it touches.
88	- HPL contract assignment, termination and expiration report: Produce the report from a saved Global Contracts query on a fixed schedule and send it to a self-managed distribution list instead of Cheryl Dudley compiling and emailing it by hand.. Why: The mail never shows the report being compiled by hand rather than printed from Global Contracts, so the 25 to 30 minutes saved per report has no support. Only two distinct issues appear (2133.eml repeats 211.eml), and the same idea was already rejected in decisions.md for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how the report is produced (hand compilation or a Global printout) and how long it takes, more issues to set the real frequency, and add or remove requests for the distribution list.
89	- Monthly industrial buyback and deficiency lists: Record buyback, swing and deficiency terms on Sitara deal tickets and run one monthly Sitara report in place of the hand-kept lists. Why: The mail shows two lists, not three: the scheduler's buyback list and the industrial 'Buyback & Deficiency Deals' worksheet are the same document. 601.eml suggests buyback status is already noted on deal tickets. 1253.eml ties the late buyback and swing setup to pathing work, not to comparing lists. So the 130 minutes a month and the day-1 setup claim are both overstated. Research that could settle it: Find what Julie Meyers' 'UPDATED SPREADSHEET' actually contains and whether it was already the source for the scheduler's worksheet, whether Sitara tickets already hold buyback terms, and how many months the worksheet was really produced; then re-estimate only the scheduler's monthly rebuild, likely 30-45 minutes.

Bill, your approval is requested.....

As I'm sure you're all aware, it took the group a day or two to hit its stride after EOL was launched on Aug. 20. We have already received approximately 30 disputes filed by various counterparties regarding deals that flowed on the 20th and 21st. Many of these will be especially difficult to settle correctly given the fact there is virtually no documentation or information to be found about the original deal. Some deals done on EOL were altered; other bilateral trades were simply zeroed out; and still others exist only in the Inc sheets. 

This situation outlines the extreme importance of documenting changes in deals as they're being made. If you have reason to zero out a trade done by an earlier shift, or to alter a trade executed online, please convey that reason. Some suggestions:

1. If you have a notebook, and use it, please enter the date on the top of the page every time you start a shift. Without that, your notes are pretty much worthless.

2. Type a short note into the Scheduling Comments section of deals you zero out or change, especially if you're changing them much later than the time they were entered.

3. Use the superfluity of spreadsheets, discussion databases, reports, Enpower applications, cut sheets, and other pieces of paper available to the Real Time group as evidence of your activity while on shift.

If this sounds unreasonable, I would welcome suggestions for an alternative. Thanks for your help.

Kate

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection in `decisions.md`. The idea itself is plausible. The problem is that the mail doesn't back up the claims about how often the report goes out or how long it takes. Other critics have already rejected this same idea twice (items 73 and 88 in `decisions.md`), and this version doesn't fix what they flagged.

What's wrong:

1. **The frequency is wrong.** Each report is named for a month: "03/01 … Report" (2114.eml) and "04/01 … Report" (211.eml). The 8 March issue was a one-off catch-up. Dudley writes that she "accidentally failed to do the report for March 2001" because the February revision ran late. The regular report then went out on 23 March "in preparation for Bid Week." So the normal pattern is one report a month, before bid week. Nothing in the mail supports the proposed mid-month run, and 2133.eml is a copy of 211.eml, not a third issue.
2. **The mail never shows the report being built by hand.** No message says whether Dudley compiles it manually or prints it straight from Global Contracts. If it's already a printout, the 40 minutes of compiling and the 35 minutes saved have no basis.
3. **The list-maintenance time isn't supported.** The only evidence is her standing line asking people to email or phone in changes. No actual requests to be added or removed appear, so the 5 minutes per report is a guess.
4. **The missed report isn't caused by the manual process.** It happened once, as a side effect of a late revision. That's a fair point to mention, but it doesn't show a recurring cost.

At the supported rate of one report a month, even the proposal's own 35 minutes comes to only about $50 a month. That figure is still unsupported until the second point is settled.

What could settle it is more evidence, not a different idea:
- mail showing how the report is produced (built by hand or printed from Global Contracts) and how long it takes;
- more issues of the report, to pin down the real frequency;
- actual requests to be added to or removed from the distribution list.

Without these, a resubmission will be rejected for the same reasons.

The rejection is in `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-4\proposals\hpl-ate-report-reject.json`.

input.prompt:
Proposal: Replace settlements' monthly round of calls and emails to the regional risk leads ("any new book codes?") with a standard TAGG report, run before NYMEX invoicing, that lists every book code that is new or that held its first financial third-party deal that month.

TODAY: Financial settlements (Rebecca Ford's group) invoices NYMEX-settled financial deals at month-end by book code. Books that are new, or that newly start holding third-party financial deals, have been missed. After four were found by accident in the August 2000 close, Ford set up a manual procedure: before each month's NYMEX invoicing, Beatrice Reyna contacts Reporting and the regional risk leads (East, Central, West, Texas) to ask about new books. The leads pass the question on to whoever covers the desk.
Evidence:
- corpus/giron-d/sent/556.eml. Ford (Aug 15 2000): "During the August settlement period, we discovered at least 4 book codes that had just recently started containing financial, third-party deals in them. We tried to put a procedure into place where we were calling the risk guys to find out about new books. I don't know, however, if we are calling the right people because we were not told about the 4 books that we discovered on our own." and "From now on, I am going to have Beatrice Reyna from my group call someone from Reporting (Frank) and key people in Risk before we run our NYMEX invoices at the end of the month." and "Even if the book codes are not brand new, but if they have just started putting financial deals in them, WE NEED TO KNOW ABOUT THEM."
- Same file, Oct 26 2000: Reyna to Keiser, Gossett and Baumbach: "Does anybody have any new book codes? Also, if anyone knows who Kyle Etter's replacement is, please let me know." Gossett forwards it to Kelly and Giron. Giron: "You can start asking me about the West desk. We don't have any new books for this month."
This shows the poll recurring monthly, being relayed (Reyna → Gossett → Giron/Kelly), mostly ending in "nothing new", and depending on a contact list that goes stale as people change roles.

input.prompt:
Proposal: Replace the nightly hand-run "official post ID" macros on each gas risk desk, and the daily list of un-officialized books that Michael Moscoso keeps, with one system check that runs after the nightly calc and alerts each book owner by name when a calculated book or post ID is not official, including post IDs with no net position.

TODAY: Each gas desk must officialize every book and post ID nightly. After a missed book put the West desk on a list that goes to Sally Beck and is reviewed weekly by Rick Buy, each desk was told to set up its own control. Dutch Quigley circulated an Excel macro that queries official books by portfolio and book code. Each desk's last person out must run it every night, and regional controllers also get an end-of-night sheet. Separately, Moscoso tracks un-officialized books every day for the Beck/Buy list. The existing benchmark check misses post IDs with no net position.
Evidence:
- corpus/giron-d/sent/595.eml (Oct 16 2000), Moscoso: "We have been tracking books that are not officialized on a daily basis. This list goes to Sally Beck and is reviewed at the end of each week by Rick Buy." … "It is imperative that we take extra care to ensure that all books are marked official each night before going home. A control process should be implemented immediately to absolutely avoid being on the list." Moscoso: "Darron Giron didn't officialize the West-NW-GDL book on Friday." Giron: "The reason my mistake was not caught on the benchmark signoff procedure is that the postid in question did not have a net position." … "If a postid has a net position and is not officialized, it will be caught using this procedure. It will not, however, if the postid does not have a position."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/586.eml: Gossett forwards Moscoso's note to 5 regional leads (Giron, Keiser, Kelly, Quigley, Baumbach). Giron to his 5 book admins: "Please make sure we stay off the "list"."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/582.eml (Oct 17 2000), Quigley to the 5 leads: "To run this file all that has to be done is enter the date and have the Portfolio and Book CD entered in also." Giron: "The macro in this file will query all official books for given Portfolio and Book codes. Use it to make sure all your postid's that need to be, are officialized each night."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/533.eml (Nov 2 2000), Giron: "Let's make sure we are doing this every night. I think Jason has been running the official post id macro most nights, but we need to have the last person finished do it every day." Gossett to Beck: "Each book adm. now checks his/her own positions that are going into V@R" and "All regional controllers will receive a sheet at the end of the night, verifying that all books are officialized."

CHANGE: The risk system (ERMS/TDS) runs a scheduled query after the nightly calc window. It lists every post ID and book that calculated that day but is not marked official, whether or not it has a net position, and sends it immediately to that book's admin and regional lead, with an escalation if still open at a cut-off. The same output feeds the Beck/Buy list automatically.

AFTER: No per-desk macro runs, no end-of-night verification sheet built by hand, no separate manual tracking by Moscoso. The zero-position gap that let the West-NW-GDL miss through is closed. People act only when the alert fires.

ESTIMATE (conservative): About 5 gas regions (West, Central, East, Texas, plus Quigley's) each run the macro nightly, entering date/portfolio/book codes and reviewing: about 3 min each = 15 min. Moscoso's daily tracking for the Beck/Buy list: about 5 min. The regional controllers' end-of-night sheet: about 5 min. Total about 25 min per trading night, less about 2 min to handle the occasional alert = about 23 min × 21 trading days ≈ 480 min/month ≈ 8 h × $85 ≈ $680/month. If you count only Giron's West desk, which is the only one whose nightly run is shown, it is about 3 min × 21 ≈ 63 min ≈ $90/month, plus Moscoso's daily tracking (5 × 21 = 105 min, about $150).

No instruction-like text was found in the cited messages.

Each desk's last person out must run it every night, and regional controllers also get an end-of-night sheet. Separately, Moscoso tracks un-officialized books every day for the Beck/Buy list. The existing benchmark check misses post IDs with no net position.
Evidence:
- corpus/giron-d/sent/595.eml (Oct 16 2000), Moscoso: "We have been tracking books that are not officialized on a daily basis. This list goes to Sally Beck and is reviewed at the end of each week by Rick Buy." … "It is imperative that we take extra care to ensure that all books are marked official each night before going home. A control process should be implemented immediately to absolutely avoid being on the list." Moscoso: "Darron Giron didn't officialize the West-NW-GDL book on Friday." Giron: "The reason my mistake was not caught on the benchmark signoff procedure is that the postid in question did not have a net position." … "If a postid has a net position and is not officialized, it will be caught using this procedure. It will not, however, if the postid does not have a position."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/586.eml: Gossett forwards Moscoso's note to 5 regional leads (Giron, Keiser, Kelly, Quigley, Baumbach). Giron to his 5 book admins: "Please make sure we stay off the "list"."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/582.eml (Oct 17 2000), Quigley to the 5 leads: "To run this file all that has to be done is enter the date and have the Portfolio and Book CD entered in also." Giron: "The macro in this file will query all official books for given Portfolio and Book codes. Use it to make sure all your postid's that need to be, are officialized each night."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/533.eml (Nov 2 2000), Giron: "Let's make sure we are doing this every night. I think Jason has been running the official post id macro most nights, but we need to have the last person finished do it every day." Gossett to Beck: "Each book adm. now checks his/her own positions that are going into V@R" and "All regional controllers will receive a sheet at the end of the night, verifying that all books are officialized."

CHANGE: The risk system (ERMS/TDS) runs a scheduled query after the nightly calc window. It lists every post ID and book that calculated that day but is not marked official, whether or not it has a net position, and sends it immediately to that book's admin and regional lead, with an escalation if still open at a cut-off. The same output feeds the Beck/Buy list automatically.

AFTER: No per-desk macro runs, no end-of-night verification sheet built by hand, no separate manual tracking by Moscoso. The zero-position gap that let the West-NW-GDL miss through is closed. People act only when the alert fires.

ESTIMATE (conservative): About 5 gas regions (West, Central, East, Texas, plus Quigley's) each run the macro nightly, entering date/portfolio/book codes and reviewing: about 3 min each = 15 min. Moscoso's daily tracking for the Beck/Buy list: about 5 min. The regional controllers' end-of-night sheet: about 5 min. Total about 25 min per trading night, less about 2 min to handle the occasional alert = about 23 min × 21 trading days ≈ 480 min/month ≈ 8 h × $85 ≈ $680/month. If you count only Giron's West desk, which is the only one whose nightly run is shown, it is about 3 min × 21 ≈ 63 min ≈ $90/month, plus Moscoso's daily tracking (5 × 21 = 105 min, about $150).

No instruction-like text was found in the cited messages.

corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-60-credit department also receives our information.  Market risk and credit risk

corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-67-differences are between credit and market risk - you all know this, but many 
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-68-of your ba's don't. 
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-69-when a book is flat it still has an effect on credit.  Flat books must be 
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml:70:officialized
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-71-market risk is keyed off positions and curves.  When we make money, market 
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-72-risk is reduced.  Credit risk is keyed off positions with customers.  When we 
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-73-make money, credit risk is increased, as people owe us more money.
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-74-
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-75-how the credit system uses RisktRAC differently from market risk
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml:76:Market risk picks up all officialized books.  If a book is not officialized 
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-77-it does not pick the book up.
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml:78:Credit picks up all officalized books.  If a book is not officialized, it 
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-79-picks up the previous day's position.  Therefore, if positions in book A are 
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml:80:moved to book B, and A is no longer officialized, credit picks up the 
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-81-previous day's position for book A.  As a result, if a book is no longer 
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml:82:used, please officialize it the first day it is no longer used, so credit 
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-83-will pick up 0 on a go forward basis.
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-84-Market risk is not concerned with counterparty codes and names.
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-85-Credit needs correct counterparty codes and names.  In recent months, the 
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml:86:counterparty information has deteriorated.  Enron official counterparty names 
corpus\giron-d\sent\401.eml-87-need to be used so they flow properly to credit.

From: Richard Tomaski@ENRON on 02/21/2001 11:42 AM
To: James Simpson/HOU/ECT@ECT, Kevin Radous
cc: Gregg Penman, Darron C Giron/HOU/ECT@ECT, Mark Mixon, Kay 
Classen/NA/Enron@Enron, Lee Fascetti, Paul Burgener, hermannt@pecorp.com 
Subject: OneOK storage deal

Enovate sold a virtual storage service to OneOk marketing.  

Transaction parameters:
MSV = 500,000 mmbtu
Daily injection \ withdraw rights = 0-25,000
enovate's demand charge = $1.75 per MSV mmbtu
Commodity charges = none
Term: Apr01 - Mar02
Location: People's Citygate



As we all know, our risk managment systems will not handle this kind of a 
transaction without al ot of manual manipulation. Below are my 
recommendations for booking this transaction.

1.  enovate should book the expected usage pattern based on the current 
market curve with a zero price (and hedge, if the trader wants) in enovate's 
MTM risk books.  The trader should periodically adjust this usage pattern as 
market conditions change.  The negative fallout from this expected usage 
should be applied against the demand charge.
 
2. As Oneok actually withdraws or injects gas into the virtual storage, we 
should record the transaction in Sitara and adjust our expected usage deal.  
The trader can hedge this position financially, physically or may be able to 
use the PGL Hub.

3. The demand charge should be booked in Tagg & Sitara and offset with 
financial annuity so we will not realize any MTM gain on the demand charge.  
We will adjust this financial annuity as losses are incurred.  Once the 
annuity is all used up, we will take all losses as incurred.  Any annuity 
amount left over at completion of the program will be taken as a gain at that 
time.

4.  This deal will be managed in the EMW book eventhough the actual 
injections\withdraws will be recorded in the enovate book.  The enovate 
physcial book will be flat - in and out at a zero price.

Cost of Carry should work in our favor unless they elect to go negative 
early.  All cash requirement should fall out in our EMW books.

Jim will build a model to determine the expected usage and track his related 
hedges (This will be similar to what Lee has, but not as complicated)

This is not intended to be a comprehensive description of how to book this 
transaction, only an outline what I believe should be reflected in our 
books.  Please forward any questions or comments to me.  Thanks.

Richard

content.text:
I rejected this proposal because it duplicates one that is already saved. The idea and the evidence were mostly sound. But another critic had already saved the same work, from the same message, as decision 13 in `decisions.md`: "Month-end poll of Risk for new book codes before NYMEX invoicing" ($35.70 a month). That entry proposes the same automatic month-end report of new books and books that newly hold third-party financial deals. The `check` command refused it for the same reason. More research would not change this.

Before I found the duplicate, I checked the claims against the mail and corrected a few points. These only matter if the proposal is reused somewhere:
- **Only one occurrence.** `corpus/giron-d/sent/556.eml` is the only message in the archive where the poll happens. "Recurring monthly" rests on Ford's stated procedure ("before we run our NYMEX invoices at the end of the month"), not on repeated messages.
- **"Mostly ending in nothing new" goes too far.** Only one reply appears in the mail, Giron's ("We don't have any new books for this month").
- **Three leads were asked in October 2000, not four.** Reyna wrote to Keiser, Gossett and Baumbach because the East lead (Kyle Etter) had left and she didn't know who replaced him. There is no message to Reporting (Frank) that month; that contact was only planned.
- **The estimate was a bit high.** Each answer is short (Gossett's forward has no text, Giron's reply is one line), so I put the saving at about 20 minutes a month rather than 25. That works out to about $28 a month.
- **Unrelated message.** The Aquila Canada message about deals missing from the April 2001 invoice (`corpus/giron-d/sent/108.eml`) is about deals in the wrong book, not new books. It doesn't support this proposal.
